title: Insured Cancellation and Return Premium under Manufactured Home Insurance
content:
Cancelling a Manufactured Home Insurance policy is the insured's own act, effective no earlier than the date of the request. The premium returned depends on when the cancellation takes effect and on who cancels.

## Return premium rules

1. **Within the free-look period.** A cancellation effective within the form's free-look period of the effective date returns all premium paid except the policy fee.
2. **After the free-look period (insured cancellation).** Otherwise the unearned premium is computed pro rata on the days remaining in the term, less the form's short-rate penalty percentage of that unearned amount, and the premium retained is never less than the form's minimum earned premium.
3. **Cancellation by the carrier.** A cancellation by the carrier, including non-renewal mid-term, returns unearned premium pro rata without penalty.
4. **Credit balance.** A credit balance left after return premium is refunded to whoever paid it — the insured, or the Hearthstone Home Finance escrow when it paid the premium.

## The quantities in rule 2, defined

- **Days in force** — the calendar days of coverage used in the term, counted from the effective date of the current term to the cancellation date, counting the effective date and not the cancellation date.
- **Pro-rata unearned premium** — the annual premium multiplied by the days remaining (365 less the days in force) and divided by 365, rounded to the cent.
- **Short-rate return** — the pro-rata unearned premium less the short-rate penalty percentage of it, rounded to the cent; but never more than the annual premium less the minimum earned premium. The return is the lower of those two amounts.

The return premium is credited on the cancellation date. Where Hearthstone Home Finance is loss payee when coverage ends, the insurance status recorded on the Hearthstone home loan becomes lapsed.

## Worked examples (hypothetical policies; short-rate penalty 10%, minimum earned premium $100.00)

| Step | Policy A | Policy B |
|---|---|---|
| Annual premium | $900 | $300 |
| Term effective date | 1 January | 1 January |
| Cancellation date | 27 May | 21 January |
| Days in force (1 January counted, cancellation date not) | 146 | 20 |
| Days remaining (365 less days in force) | 219 | 345 |
| Pro-rata unearned premium | $540.00 | $283.56 |
| Less 10% of the unearned premium, rounded to the cent | $486.00 | $255.20 |
| Annual premium less minimum earned premium | $800.00 | $200.00 |
| Return premium (the lower of the two lines above) | $486.00 | $200.00 |

In Policy B the minimum earned premium governs: $100.00 is retained and $200.00 returned.

*Free-look case (hypothetical).* An insured who paid a first installment of $100.02 and the policy fee cancels with effect 5 days after the effective date. The cancellation falls within the free-look period: the $100.02 of premium paid is returned and the policy fee is not.

*Carrier cancellation (hypothetical).* Had the carrier cancelled Policy A on 27 May, the return would be the pro-rata unearned premium of $540.00, with no penalty.

## Basis Q&A

- *Can a cancellation be back-dated before the request?* No; it is effective no earlier than the date of the request.
- *Where does a refund go when the escrow paid the premium?* To the Hearthstone Home Finance escrow.
